title: Hidden single
subtitle: The only spot for a digit

screens.text: A hidden single is a digit that fits in only one cell of a row, column or box. Here is how to find one. The top left box needs a 7. Each marked 7 rules out its own row and its own column, so 7 cannot go there. Only one empty cell in the box is left. Tap it.
screens.praise: Yes. In this box, 7 fits in only one cell. That is a hidden single.

wrong.text: 7 cannot go there. That row already has a 7. Find the empty cell in the box that no 7 rules out.
7 cannot go there. That column already has a 7. Find the empty cell in the box that no 7 rules out.
That cell already holds a digit. Find the empty cell in the box where 7 fits.
That is one of the 7s. It rules out its own row and column. Find the empty cell in the box where 7 still fits.
That cell is outside the top left box. Find the empty cell in that box where 7 fits.
First find the cell. Tap the empty cell in the top left box where 7 fits.
Stay in Place mode. Tap the empty cell in the top left box where 7 fits.

screens.fallback: Tap the empty cell in the top left box where 7 fits.

screens.text: We crossed out every digit this cell's row, column and box already have. 2, 5, 7 and 8 are still open, so the ring alone cannot tell which one goes here. But 7 has no other place in this box. So this cell must be 7. Tap 7.
screens.praise: Well done. A hidden single can hide among other open digits, so look at one digit at a time.

wrong.text: {d} is still open, but that only means nothing rules it out yet. 7 has no other place in this box. Tap 7.
{d} has an X, because this cell's row, column or box already has a {d}. Tap 7.
This cell is ready. Tap 7 on the number pad.
Keep this cell selected. Tap 7 on the number pad.
Stay in Place mode. Tap 7 on the number pad.

screens.text: A hidden single works in a row too. The marked row needs a 6. Remember, a 6 rules out its own row, column and box. The marked 6s rule out every empty cell in this row but one. Tap that cell, then tap 6.

next.start: Find the empty cell in the marked row where 6 fits, tap it, then tap 6.

screens.praise: Right. In this row, 6 fits in only one cell.

screens.text: And in a column. The marked column needs a 3. Look for the 3s on the board. They rule out every empty cell in this column but one. Tap that cell, then tap 3.

screens.praise: Yes. In this column, 3 fits in only one cell.

screens.text: Here is a tip. Tap a digit on the board, and every copy of that digit lights up. Then you can see at a glance which rows, columns and boxes already have it. Tap the marked 5.
screens.praise: See all the 5s light up? Use this trick whenever you hunt for a hidden single.

screens.text: Your turn. Look at the 5s. One box has only one empty cell left where 5 can go. Find that cell, tap it, then tap 5.

next.start: Find the box where 5 fits in just one empty cell, tap that cell, then tap 5.

screens.praise: You found a hidden single on your own. With this and the last empty cell, you can solve every Beginner puzzle.
